set-a/method.md: The scientific method is neither a sequence of steps nor a demand for a citation.
Who proposed a claim and where it came from therefore carry no weight:
A citation is the address of someone else's test and never the support itself.
A rule of a skill is a prescription, and a prescription follows from a goal joined with the claim that the technique serves it, never from facts alone.
No single criterion separates science from the rest, so the method takes what the main lines of the philosophy of science agree on and applies it to every statement alike.
A logical inference is worth what its premises are worth and forms no kind of its own.
The author's name and the standing of the venue support nothing.
A claim of our own that has no citation takes the lowest branches:
set-a/README.md: research any topic with source verification, map its complete question space before you start, then write AI agent context that actually works — grounded instructions and disciplined reasoning instead of vibes.
Rooted admits rules by the scientific method instead:
- **Tested, not asserted.** A rule that claims a technique works rests on a test that could have refuted it — a study opened and read, or a test of our own committed to the repository.
A citation is the address of such a test, and where an idea came from carries no weight.
The method here is neither a sequence of steps nor a demand for a citation:
A citation is the address of someone else's test and never the support itself;
A claim of our own needs no citation.
the philosophy of science offers no single criterion of what is scientific, so the method takes what its main lines agree on.
the lines not yet touched carry their sources without a record.
